newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST-Experts eye ECI, NAPM, jobs in 10/28 week.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Experts eye ECI, NAPM, jobs in 10/28 week.

text.p: If this week's sparse economic calendar caused hunger pains, next week's smorgasbord of data may induce indigestion.

If the 15 key data items scheduled for release next week seem too much to digest, experts in a Reuters poll recommend a diet including the Employment Cost Index (ECI), the National Association of Purchasing Manager's (NAPM) index and payrolls.
"It's a lot there," said Astrid Adolfson, senior economist at MCM MoneyWatch, referring to next week's slew of data.
She said ECI bears close watching because, "that's the one the (Federal Reserve) likes best of all the wage measures."
On average 26 economists forecast the ECI rose 0.8 percent in the third quarter, the same as in the previous quarter.

Peter Kretzmer, senior economist at Nationsbanc Capital Markets Inc, said the market may get a little exercised over the ECI, but the number is "a little less crucial now, with the Fed more clearly happy" holding short-term interest rates than it was last quarter.
The ECI is scheduled for release on Tuesday, October 29 at 0830 EST/1330 GMT.
Jobs data and the NAPM index are both set for release on Friday, November 1.
"The unemployment claims numbers suggest that September was an aberration, so we get a bounce back," said John Ryding, senior economist at Bear, Stearns and Co Inc.
On average, experts forecast October payrolls rose 212,000, a sharp increase from a 40,000 decline in September.
The economists forecast the NAPM October manufacturing activity index dropped to 51.0 from 51.7 the prior month.
